actorIndex.description: Registered index callback truncates argument to unsigned byte, compares against signed active count, requires actor+1fc bit1 and either bit1000 or actor+406 byte3. A nonzero actor+28b requires actor+1010 float strictly greater than0. Returns the reference record itself without its first-pointer dereference.

refresh.description: Null set, absent index callback or nonpositive signed-byte count is a no-op. Owner bytes255 and128 are preserved sentinels. Other owners resolve through actual43c7a0. Missing/invalid actor, missing packet or missing selected locator yields selected byte255; otherwise truncate the signed locator-pointer difference divided by60 to its low byte. Mismatch with set index writes owner255. Selected locator and actor reservation token are never cleared here. A set index255 can therefore preserve an invalid owner.

release.description: First call only. Default target is creature+d0 reference then its first-pointer world object. Every ordered case-insensitive character= substring replaces that target through the actual name callback; missing callback/name clears it and last token wins. A nonnull target receives zero at actor+36c. The packet+a4 selected locator stays unchanged.

breakFormation.description: If creature and its+144 formation are nonnull, clear only bit8 at formation+50. No first-call guard; always returns1. The typed formation projection does not infer behavior of downstream movement or formation allocation.

native.method: Original command, index callback, reservation refresh and actual name binding execute unchanged. Only bounded CRT Player%d formatting is substituted. Complete actor, packet, owner and formation memory images are checked for collateral writes.

limits: Valid nonoverlapping actor/packet/set/formation storage; selected locator indices represent aligned pointers relative to one locator base, no address wrap.
ASCII names, finite death timer, active table backing valid for every reachable index; count and set count preserve signed comparisons.
Managed replay is prepared and compiled, not executed.
